verdict.rationale: Honeybadger lets users configure some rule-based background behavior. Alarms run BadgerQL queries against thresholds and trigger alerts, integrations can be set to create notifications or tickets on chosen error events, and errors auto-resolve when a deploy is recorded. These are narrow alerting and housekeeping rules rather than general autonomous automations; the Cursor Automations webhook relies on an external platform's automation and earns no credit. Missing for 10: a general-purpose user-defined automation or workflow builder, autonomous actions beyond alerts, ticketing and auto-resolve, agent-driven background tasks, and independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: Alarms combine a BadgerQL query (“count all slow requests in the past five minutes”) with a threshold (“when count is > 2”) and trigger alerts when the query result exceeds the threshold.
You get to choose which error events result in a notification or ticket being created
By default, all unresolved errors are automatically marked as resolved when a deployment is recorded
